newsitem.title: USA: Senators urge more low-income heating assistance.
newsitem.headline: Senators urge more low-income heating assistance.

text.p: Two senators called on President Clinton Friday to release $420 million in emergency funds to help low-income people heat their homes following recent price hikes in several types of heating fuels.

Cold weather and high fuel prices are stretching resources of the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Programme (LIHEAP), and regular allocations to states "are clearly going to be insufficient to meet minimal needs," Pennsylvania Republican Arlen Specter and Iowa Democrat Tom Harkin said in a letter to Clinton.

Specter, chairman of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Health and Human Services, and Harkin, the panel's ranking Democrat, in their letter said emergency funds should be released now "in time to allow for the delivery of additional fuel before many elderly and low income families reach the bottom of their tanks in the middle of winter."

"With the sharp price rise in fuel oil, natural gas and propane, fuel assistance checks are meeting even less of the need than we had hoped and the funding shortfalls are placing many people at risk," Harkin said in a statement.
LIHEAP provides funds to states to help low-income households meet their fuel bills during the winter.
